title: Equivalence of Counterfactual Conditional Independence Theories under Restricted Hard Interventions
banked_reason: The promised bow-allowed-ADMG original-graph characterization and world hierarchy remain open; the delivered Markovian-DAG subclass substitutes the advertised kernel.
gap_reasons: The promised bow-allowed-ADMG original-graph characterization/canonicalization is not delivered: this node explicitly leaves completeness open, while prop:dag-global-criterion proves only the Markovian-DAG subclass.
The promised determination of whether two worlds suffice or a strict hierarchy exists for bow-allowed ADMGs remains an open question here; the two-world result is only for Markovian DAGs.
proof_attempt_summary: The run derived and reviewed a complete finite Markovian-DAG criterion, a sharp two-world DAG bound, local covered-reversal and isolated-bow equivalences, fair-bit countermodels, and a finite semantic decision upper bound. It failed because the advertised bow-allowed ADMG kernel still lacked both a complete syntactic original-graph criterion and a certified two-world reduction or strict-hierarchy splitter; a proposed semantic truth-table replacement was rejected as tautological. A future attempt should reuse the sound DAG and local-bow results only if it brings a genuinely new ADMG completeness mechanism.
tldr: For finite pairwise-root SCMs under hard interventions on a fixed proper set \(A\), the target is equality of universal same-unit counterfactual CI theories. On Markovian DAGs, the descendant region, all parent sets entering it, and the ordinary Markov-equivalence class of the unaffected complement form a complete original-graph signature; two raw worlds are uniformly sufficient and sharp when \(A\) is nonempty. An isolated covered bow also yields a nontrivial full-law equivalence. A fair-bit witness reduction gives a crude doubly exponential decision upper bound. A complete consistency-aware separator, original-graph canonicalization, and sharp world or complexity boundary for bow-allowed ADMGs remain open.
gap: Existing results solve adjacent but different problems: ordinary ADMG Markov equivalence, equivalence of tuples of hard-interventional distributions, individual-query AMWN separation, physical realizability of a specified counterfactual distribution, identification of a target from available Layer-3 distributions, and counterfactual equivalence of fully specified SCMs. None inspected characterizes equality of universal, consistency-aware same-unit counterfactual CI theories of graph-compatible SCM classes under a fixed proper manipulable set.
fill: Establish a support-safe complete query criterion, prove the proposed DAG signature or find its first counterexample, and then derive a complete ADMG canonicalization/move system or a sharp complexity obstruction. In parallel, settle two-world sufficiency versus a certified hierarchy.
